summary: Master's and PhD scholarship for non-Chinese applicants admitted to the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS) or the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC). Applicants apply through the UCAS or USTC admission portal and select the CAS-ANSO Scholarship; PhD applicants tick a box to be considered for the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship. Master's applicants must be born on or after 1 January 1996 and PhD applicants on or after 1 January 1991. Applicants need English or Chinese proficiency and must meet the admission criteria of the university. Current master's students in China cannot apply for the master's programme and current doctoral students in China cannot apply for the PhD. Applying to both USTC and UCAS is not allowed. The 2026 evaluation has finished; no 2027 call was listed on the ANSO site when checked.
route_name: Online application via UCAS or USTC admission portal
deadline_source_text: 31 January 2026 (Beijing Time) for applicants and referees; the call opened 15 October 2025. No time of day is stated.

programme_title: Chinese Government Scholarship - Silk Road Program
intake_term: 2026 intake (Huazhong University of Science and Technology notice)
funding_summary: As described in the Huazhong University of Science and Technology (HUST) notice: tuition waiver, accommodation, a monthly stipend of CNY 2,500 and comprehensive medical insurance of CNY 800 a year. Stipends and benefits vary by level and university.
summary: Full-scholarship programme for students from Belt and Road countries, run by individual Chinese universities. This entry records the 2026 HUST notice for undergraduate Software Engineering (4 years) and Architecture (5 years), taught in Chinese. HUST requires citizenship of Russia, Malaysia, Mongolia, Laos, Indonesia, Cambodia, Thailand, Bangladesh, Vietnam or Pakistan, a high school diploma with excellent results, age under 25 (born after 1 September 2001), HSK 4 with a score of at least 180, and a CSCA report in Professional Chinese, Maths and Physics. Applicants apply on the HUST system, pay an application fee of CNY 600 (or USD 100), then apply in the Chinese Government Scholarship Information System as Program Category B with the university's agency number. Other universities publish their own Silk Road notices with different countries, levels and deadlines.
source_publisher: Huazhong University of Science and Technology, International Students Office
route_name: Apply to the host university (HUST system), then register in the CSC system as Type B
deadline_source_text: 20 May 2026 at HUST. No time or time zone stated. Other universities set their own deadlines.

programme_title: Chinese Government Scholarship - University Program (Type B)
intake_term: 2026 intake (Shanghai University of Finance and Economics notice)
funding_summary: As described in the Shanghai University of Finance and Economics (SUFE) notice: full tuition waiver, on-campus accommodation fees, a monthly living allowance (RMB 3,000 master's, RMB 3,500 doctoral) and comprehensive medical insurance. Duration 2 years for master's and 3 or 4 years for doctoral.
teaching_language: Chinese or English (depends on the programme)
summary: Type B scholarships are selected and enrolled by Chinese universities, which nominate candidates to the China Scholarship Council. This entry records the 2026 SUFE notice. Applicants first apply to a SUFE graduate programme and pay the application fee, then after a conditional offer apply in the Chinese Government Scholarship Information System choosing Type B and SUFE's agency number 10272. SUFE then nominates top candidates to the CSC for expert review. Eligibility: non-Chinese citizens in good health with a valid foreign passport; master's applicants generally under 35 and doctoral applicants under 40. English-taught programmes need TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 110; Chinese-taught programmes need HSK 5 with a score of at least 180. Other universities publish their own Type B guides and agency numbers.
source_publisher: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, International Students
route_name: Apply to the host university, then register in the CSC system as Type B
deadline_source_text: Stage 1 (programme application) 16 November 2025 to 28 February 2026; conditional offers and the scholarship application in late March 2026; results late June or July 2026. All times Beijing time. Other universities set their own dates.

programme_title: Peking University Scholarships for International Graduate Students (CSC, PKUS, BGS)
funding_summary: The notice gives no cash amounts. CSC: full or partial tuition waiver, living stipend, housing and medical insurance. PKUS (Peking University Scholarship): full or partial tuition waiver, living stipend and medical insurance. BGS (Beijing Government Scholarship): full or partial tuition waiver. Duration 2 to 3 years for master's and 4 to 5 years for doctoral (PKUS doctoral 4 years).
summary: One PKU application is considered for three scholarships: the Chinese Government Scholarship for the Advanced Graduate Program, the Peking University Scholarship and the Beijing Government Scholarship. Applicants must meet PKU's admission requirements and submit a 2026 full-time self-funded graduate application. Applicants apply on the PKU International Student Service System; the CSC scholarship also needs a separate application in the CSC system (institution code 10001, application type B, one major only). Applicants who already hold other Chinese government or PKU scholarships, apart from one-time merit awards, are not eligible, and applicants in joint training programmes are excluded. Decisions are expected by email around July and August.
source_publisher: Peking University, International Students and Scholars Services
route_name: Online application (PKU International Student Service System)
deadline_source_text: PKU online application: 9:00 a.m. on 9 March (Beijing Time); CSC application: midnight on 17 March. The notice is dated 12 January 2026 and states no year beside the dates.

summary: 75 fellowships in total, 27 open for new recruitment, for nationals of 135 invited developing UNESCO Member States. Levels: one-year Visiting Scholar programmes (General or Senior) and Master's or Doctoral degrees of 2 to 5 years; no bachelor's degrees, although high school diploma holders may join the one-year General Scholar programme. Age limits at September 2026 enrolment: General Scholar 45, Senior Scholar 50, master's 35, doctoral 40. Applicants must first obtain a pre-admission letter from a Chinese university, register in the Chinese Government Scholarship Information System (agency number 00001, Type A), and submit to their country's National Commission for UNESCO; individuals cannot apply to UNESCO directly. The page was last updated after the deadlines while still saying applications were open, so confirm the status with your National Commission.

deadline_source_text: Candidates submit to their National Commission by 23 January 2026; National Commissions nominate to UNESCO by 10 February 2026; no notification by 15 August 2026 means unsuccessful. No time or time zone stated.
